name: LargeRDFBench Interoperable Edition
description: LargeRDFBench Interoperable Edition A drop-in replacement for the data and expected results of LargeRDFBench, the billion-triple benchmark for SPARQL endpoint federation (Saleem et al., Journal of Web Semantics, 2018). Several of the original data dumps violate the RDF specifications, so engines with strict parsers cannot load them, and the expected results ship in an ad hoc format. This edition repairs both. The benchmark itself is unchanged: no triple is added or removed, no query is rewritten — only malformed terms are corrected and serialisations normalised. Triple counts per dataset are preserved, so results obtained here stay comparable to results reported against the original. Contents Data: 13 datasets, 1,003,960,176 triples, as valid UTF-8 N-Triples, with HDT counterparts. Queries: the full suite of 40: S1–S14 (simple), C1–C10 (complex), L1–L8 (large data), CH1–CH8 (complex + large data). Expected results: W3C SPARQL 1.1 Query Results JSON Format, with encoding defects fixed throughout and the result sets for S7, C7 and C8 corrected against the source data. What changed Malformed IRIs, literals and language tags rewritten to conform to RDF 1.1; all dumps re-serialised as valid UTF-8 N-Triples. Expected results converted from the original ad hoc format to SPARQL 1.1 Query Results JSON. Three result sets (S7, C7, C8) recomputed against the repaired data.
